title: Every finite separable extension of the completion of a discrete valuation field is obtained by base change from a finite separable extension of the field
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and completion, every finite separable extension of the completed fraction field arises by base change from a finite separable extension of K (statement lines 33813-33820). The proof combines three ingredients in one construction: a primitive element whose minimal polynomial is cleared into the completed ring, an approximation of that polynomial by a polynomial over A to within an arbitrarily high power of the maximal ideal, and Krasner's lemma, which turns the approximation into a root of the approximating polynomial inside the finite complete local algebra B, after which a Nakayama argument identifies the two quotients and the extension over K is read off (proof lines 33829-33851). The hypothesis of separability is used exactly where it is needed, namely to know that theta is not a root of the derivative so that Krasner applies. The counted span refers three times to earlier lemmas of this chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
